The second phase of the Season 1 EIGEN stakedrop is officially live! The addition of Phase 2 brings the total Season 1 distribution to about 113 million EIGEN . This represents 6.7% of the 15% of the total EIGEN supply set aside for stakedrops.

During Phase 1, the EigenLayer community demonstrated a strong commitment to the project's mission by staking and delegating over 88% of their claimed EIGEN tokens. Your enthusiastic participation showcases the community's commitment to EIGEN's vision and potential. Thank you to everyone who staked!

Stay tuned: We will announce Season 2 distribution details in the coming weeks

What Makes the EIGEN Token Unique?

EIGEN staking complements ETH restaking on EigenLayer, enhancing the security and functionality of established and emerging protocols. ETH restaking allows ETH to secure services with objectively attributable faults, provable onchain through an optimistic dispute resolution mechanism.

However, many digital tasks have faults that are not provable onchain but are observable by any honest observer. These are intersubjectively attributable faults. EIGEN staking aims to secure AVSs against these faults, providing a mechanism for a consensus of honest observers to penalize delegated EIGEN stake.

We call this mechanism “intersubjective forking.” Through EIGEN’s unique intersubjective forking mechanism, new types of services can be secured with cryptoeconomic guarantees, making EIGEN a powerful tool for building both more secure and more versatile digital ecosystems. EIGEN staking allows Actively Validated Services (AVS) across diverse applications, such as data availability, AI inference, and decentralized storage, to accelerate their development and better ensure the reliability of their services.

To learn more about EIGEN’s innovative design, read the full EIGEN whitepaper here .

How were the Phase 2 address allocations determined?

There was three-step process for determining individual Phase 2 address allocations:

The Eigen Foundation reserved an allocation for each LRT protocol based on its interactions with the EigenLayer protocol. For these LRT protocol allocations, we followed the same criteria as Phase 1. No penalty was applied.

The specific allocation provided for your address was determined by the relevant LRT protocol. Each LRT protocol produced its own allocation list with respect to its end users.

The Eigen Foundation conducted a sybil analysis and risk analysis to finalize the eligible addresses and their corresponding claims.

Claim Window: Open now through September 7, 2024.

Bonus: All Season 1 users will receive the 100 EIGEN bonus, including the Phase 2 users. However, no user will receive the bonus twice.

How to Claim:

Visit: claims.eigenfoundation.org

Follow the instructions to claim, stake and delegate your EIGEN.

Important Details:

Phase 2 Allocation: Each participating Liquid Restaking Token (LRT) project determines the distribution based on your specific interactions with their protocol. Additionally, the Eigen Foundation conducted compliance checks and Sybil detection on the LRT-provided distributions.

Contact: For questions regarding your eligibility or allocation, contact the LRT project(s) you interacted with.

Staking & Delegating: Stake and Delegate your EIGEN to secure EigenDA and support other AVSs. EigenLayer incorporates a 24-day delay for unstaking as a security measure, due to the novel forking mechanism of EIGEN. Similar to Ethereum and other staking protocols, this delay helps enhance network security.

Non-Transferable: EIGEN tokens are currently non-transferable. For more details, refer to this tweet.

Season 2

With the completion of Phase 2, Season 1 will have officially concluded! However, Season 2 is already underway, and distribution details will be shared in the coming weeks as part of ongoing additional distribution. Stay tuned!
